questions.q: What was the major event that caused Ashoka to change his mind about fighting wars?
questions.a: The Kalinga War. A student who answers "becoming a Buddhist" or "his father's advice" shows they are guessing based on external knowledge rather than the provided text on his personal remorse.

questions.q: Why did Ashoka feel "remorse" after the Kalinga War?
questions.a: He felt deep regret because he saw the massive loss of life and the suffering of displaced people. A student who says he lost the war shows they missed the fact that he was the victor, but the human cost changed his perspective.

questions.q: If Ashoka were a king today, how might his decision to give up war affect his relationship with his neighbors?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Identify his new goal (peace). 2. Compare with traditional war-based power. 3. Conclude that he would likely use diplomacy. A student who says he would be conquered immediately fails to understand that he remained an emperor; they are confusing "giving up war" with "giving up power."

questions.q: Compare the Ashoka before the Kalinga War to the Ashoka after it.
questions.a: Before, he was a conqueror focused on expansion; after, he was a ruler focused on non-violence and avoiding conflict. A student who fails to see the contrast suggests they do not understand the concept of a "turning point."

questions.q: Was Ashoka's decision to stop fighting a sign of defeat? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, it was a choice made from a position of strength after winning the war. A student who says "yes" misunderstands that Ashoka was the conqueror, not the conquered; his choice was moral, not forced.

questions.q: Imagine you are an advisor to Ashoka right after the Kalinga War. What is one peaceful way he could show his power instead of invading more land?
questions.a: A good answer would suggest building infrastructure, helping the displaced people, or focusing on internal prosperity. A poor answer would focus on more fighting, showing they have not internalized the shift in his policy.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Ashoka was the third emperor of the Mauryan Empire who, after witnessing the immense death and suffering during his conquest of Kalinga, underwent a moral ______ and renounced warfare.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever played a game where ______ felt so bad that you didn't want to play anymore?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to describe the Kalinga War as a turning point in Ashoka’s life and explain why he decided to change his policy from military conquest to non-violence.
